newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended down on Wednesday from New York's previous close, pushed lower by Tokyo sales and early producer selling, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$323.60/324.10 per ounce compared to New York's close at US$325.30 on Tuesday.
"It's two-way trade in a very mixed market. It's not a very strong market but people can make some profits as the price is not moving too fast," said one dealer.
Traders in Tokyo were buying and selling gold on currency fluctuations, dealers said.
Gold rebounded slightly in early afternoon when European markets opened.
Hong Kong dealers said many trading houses still held short positions in the market.
Physical demand was quiet and buyers were watching for direction before jumping in, dealers said.
U.S. stocks, bonds and the dollar responded positively to U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress on Tuesday.
Greenspan said the recent drop in gold prices reflected falling inflationary expectations.
Local tael gold ended HK$15 lower at HK$3,003.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +1.00 from its previous fix at nil.
